entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nicholas Mesarites was a Byzantine Greek churchman and writer who rose to prominence in the 12th century.

As Metropolitan of Ephesus in the Empire of Nicaea, Mesarites played a significant role in shaping the spiritual and cultural landscape of the Byzantine Empire.

One of his most notable contributions was his involvement in the compilation of the codex of the Byzantine Empire's legal code, known as the 'Corpus Juris Civilis'.

Mesarites' legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of Eastern Orthodox theology and the preservation of Byzantine cultural heritage.

The legacy of Nicholas Mesarites can be seen in the many manuscripts and texts that have survived to this day, a testament to the enduring power of his work.

In the words of the 19th-century historian, John Henry Burt, 'The most valuable contribution of Mesarites was the collection of the Byzantine documents, the Corpus Juris Civilis, which, in its completeness and accuracy, represents the most perfect type of the juridical literature of the ancient Greeks and Romans, the true and authentic basis of the Roman law of Europe.'
